verses.text: The men of Ephraim called out their troops, crossed over to Zaphon and said to Jephthah, "Why did you go to fight the Ammonites without calling us to go with you? We are going to burn down your house with you inside!"
Jephthah answered, "My people and I were in a great struggle with the Ammonites. I called you, but you did not save me from them.
When I saw that you would not help, I took my life in my hands and crossed over to fight the Ammonites, and the LORD gave me the victory. So why have you come up today to fight me?"

Then Jephthah gathered all the men of Gilead and fought against Ephraim. The men of Gilead struck them down, because the Ephraimites had said, "You people of Gilead are just runaways from Ephraim and Manasseh."

The men of Gilead captured the river crossings of the Jordan leading to Ephraim. Whenever a runaway from Ephraim said, "Let me cross over," the men of Gilead asked, "Are you from Ephraim?" If he said, "No,"

they said, "All right, say 'Shibboleth.'" If he said "Sibboleth," because he could not say the word correctly, they grabbed him and killed him at the river crossings of the Jordan. Forty-two thousand Ephraimites were killed at that time.
Jephthah led Israel as judge for six years. Then Jephthah from Gilead died and was buried in a town in Gilead.
After him, Ibzan of Bethlehem led Israel.

He had thirty sons and thirty daughters. He gave his daughters in marriage to men outside his clan, and he brought in thirty young women from outside his clan as wives for his sons. Ibzan led Israel for seven years.
Then Ibzan died and was buried in Bethlehem.
After him, Elon from the tribe of Zebulun led Israel for ten years.
Then Elon died and was buried in Aijalon in the land of Zebulun.
After him, Abdon son of Hillel, from Pirathon, led Israel.
He had forty sons and thirty grandsons, who rode on seventy donkeys. He led Israel for eight years.
Then Abdon son of Hillel died and was buried at Pirathon in Ephraim, in the hill country of the Amalekites.
